summary.en: Turn links around while keeping the unprocessed suffix reachable.
summary.bn: বাকি নোডগুলোর অ্যাড্রেস না হারিয়ে লিংকের দিক উল্টে দাও।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Reverse with prev, cur and next
examples.explanationHtml: next saves the unprocessed suffix before cur->next changes. prev becomes the new head after cur reaches NULL.

examples.title: Reverse by returning through recursive calls
examples.explanationHtml: The final node returns as new_head. Each returning call turns its successor’s link backward and clears the old forward link.

examples.title: Reverse twice to restore the order
examples.explanationHtml: Reversal changes links rather than values. Repeating it restores both the sequence and the original first node.

practice.title: Reverse an entire chain
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Use three pointers and print the reversed List:.
hints: Keep the old successor before turning its link.

practice.title: Reverse through recursive returns
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Use recursive reversal and print List:.
hints: Clear the old head’s next field on return.

practice.title: Restore after two reversals
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Reverse twice, then print List:.
hints: Every reversed edge turns back on the second pass.

practice.title: Reverse only the first k nodes
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Read k (0..n), reverse that prefix, keep the suffix order and print List:.
hints: The old prefix head becomes the link to the untouched suffix.

quiz.prompt: At the start of iterative reversal, what is prev?
quiz.explanation: The reversed prefix is empty, so its head is NULL.

quiz.prompt: Which statement preserves the unprocessed suffix?
quiz.explanation: The original forward link is overwritten next. Saving it keeps the remaining nodes reachable.

quiz.prompt: When cur becomes NULL, which pointer is the new head?
quiz.explanation: prev heads the entire reversed prefix after all nodes have been processed.

quiz.prompt: Why set head->next = NULL during recursive unwinding?
options: To remove the old forward edge and prevent a cycle
quiz.explanation: The successor now points backward at head. Leaving head’s old edge would make a two-node cycle.

quiz.prompt: Which recursive base inputs need no link reversal?
quiz.explanation: There is no edge to reverse in either case, so the original head can be returned.

quiz.prompt: What happens to node identities after reversal?
options: The same nodes appear in reverse link order
quiz.explanation: The algorithm changes next fields. It neither copies values nor replaces allocations.

quiz.prompt: What is iterative reversal’s cost on n nodes?
options: Theta(n squared) time and O(n) extra space
Theta(n) time and O(1) extra space
quiz.explanation: Every node has its link redirected once. Three working pointers suffice.

quiz.prompt: After reversing the first edge, what does the old head’s next contain?
quiz.explanation: prev begins as NULL, so assigning cur->next=prev sets a.next to NULL. The equality prints one.

quiz.prompt: Which value heads the two-node chain after both links turn?
quiz.explanation: The first iteration turns a.next to NULL. The second sets b.next to a, leaving prev at b and order 24 12.

quiz.prompt: How many edge assignments occur for a three-node iterative reversal?
quiz.explanation: The loop executes once for each of the three modeled nodes, so changes becomes three.

quiz.prompt: Which invariant describes the two chains at each reversal loop boundary?
options: prev always equals the original head
cur always equals the final node
prev heads the reversed prefix and cur heads the untouched suffix
quiz.explanation: Every round transfers one node from the suffix to the reversed prefix while preserving their union.

quiz.prompt: A caller retains tail as persistent state. What must it become after full reversal?
quiz.explanation: The old first node ends with next=NULL and is the new last node. Empty reversal keeps both endpoints NULL.

keyPoints.en: The prev pointer owns the already reversed prefix during iteration.
keyPoints.bn: Iterative reversal-এ prev ইতিমধ্যে উল্টানো অংশের শুরু ধরে রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Save next before redirecting cur->next toward prev.
keyPoints.bn: cur->next-কে prev-এর দিকে ঘোরানোর আগে next রেখে দাও।

keyPoints.en: The old head becomes the new tail with a NULL next link.
keyPoints.bn: পুরোনো head নতুন tail হয়, আর তার next হয় NULL।

keyPoints.en: Recursive reversal returns the final node as the new head.
keyPoints.bn: Recursive reversal-এ শেষ নোডটি নতুন head হয়ে ফেরত আসে।

keyPoints.en: Iterative reversal uses constant extra space while recursion needs call frames.
keyPoints.bn: Iterative reversal-এ বাড়তি জায়গা ধ্রুব; রিকার্শনে call frame লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Trace prev, cur and next while reversing A -> B -> C -> NULL.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Initially prev=NULL and cur=A. Save B, set A.next=NULL, move prev=A and cur=B. Save C, set B.next=A, move prev=B and cur=C. Save NULL, set C.next=B, then prev=C and cur=NULL. Return C.

examQuestions.question: Write iterative reverse returning the new head.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *reverse(Node *head)
{
    Node *prev = NULL;
    Node *cur = head;
    while (cur != NULL) {
        Node *next = cur->next;
        cur->next = prev;
        prev = cur;
        cur = next;
    }
    return prev;
}

examQuestions.question: Explain why forgetting head = reverse(head) can hide most of the reversed chain.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The function returns the new head. The caller’s old head now identifies the tail with next=NULL. Ignoring the return value leaves only that tail reachable from the caller, even though the other nodes still exist. Assign the returned pointer before printing or freeing.
